newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slump 2.73 pct in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slump 2.73 pct in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended early losses in afternoon selling on Monday amid liquidity shortage as political uneasiness, first quarter results and April inflation figures irritated the market, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,392, down 39 points, or 2.73 percent from Friday, after rebounding slightly from a late low of 1,388. Daily volume dropped to 9.81 trillion lira from Friday's 10.67 trillion.

"I expect the general direction to be downward until prices bottom out or there is a positive political development. Reaction buys at the current levels will be short-lived," said Cem Baycan from Delta securities.
Brokers who await major support at the index's 1,380 level after the shattering of 1,420 and 1,400 supports today, said fresh liquidity influx was necessary for a lasting recovery.
They said sentiment soured as many companies released poor first quarter results on Monday and April consumer inflation, released on Sunday, came out above market expectations of around 5.5 percent.
Turkey's wholesale inflation was 5.5 percent and consumer inflation was 6.6 percent in April, compared to 6.0 percent and 5.4 percent, respectively in March.
The market index had dived 6.6 percent in seven days amid political worries over the fate of the Islamist-led coalition government after the market opened on April 24 following a 6-1/2 day holiday.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Saturday ruled out early elections as a solution to his dispute with the secularist army over Islamist activism.
Turkish opposition efforts to form a secularist alliance against Erbakan faltered last week and Erbakan challenged his critics to elections.
He had come under heavy fire from secularist centres led by the army for his reluctance to implement measures recommended by the army to fight rising Islamist activism.

Of the 248 shares traded, falls outdid rises sharply by 189 to 24 and 35 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial dived 3.47 percent to 1,392, the IMKB Services lost 2.89 percent to 1,277 and the IMKB Financial shed 1.69 percent to 1,512.
The leading active shares were those of synthetic fibre maker Sasa which fell 100 lira to 6,000. They made up 6.3 percent of the total turnover.
